ops.title: The Edit tool strips a trailing space from new_string — an `X` → `X ` edit silently no-ops or drops the space; never rely on a trailing space, include the following token instead
ops.body:
The **Edit tool strips a trailing space from `new_string`**. An edit whose replacement ends in a space either silently drops the space or errors with `No changes to make: old_string and new_string are exactly the same` (because after stripping, the two are identical).

This is a live landmine for any "insert a separator" rewrite. On 2026-07-14 a `replace_all` of `/.venv/bin/capt-hook run ` → `/.venv/bin/hook run ` in this repo's committed `.claude/settings.json` landed as `hook runPreToolUse` — an invalid command that exits 2, so the PreToolUse hook denied **every** tool call and the identically-broken Stop hook rejected the end of every turn. Self-repair was impossible (Edit was blocked too); the user had to fix it externally with a `!` bang-command. See [[dogfoods-own-cli-as-hooks]].

**How to apply:** never let a replacement depend on a trailing space. Include the next token in both strings (`hook runPreToolUse` → `hook run PreToolUse`), or do the rewrite with a `python3 -c` regex via Bash. And when an edit rewrites a *live* config the harness executes (settings.json hooks, launchers), dump and eyeball the resulting commands **before** the next tool call — after it goes live you may have no working tools left to fix it with.
